title: Simultaneous Noetherian local approximation of a morphism of finitely presented modules
statement:
Let $R	o S$ be a local homomorphism of commutative local rings (the inverse image of the maximal ideal of $S$ is the maximal ideal of $R$). Suppose that $S$ is a localization of a finitely presented $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let $M,N$ be finitely presented $S$-modules [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] and $u:M	o N$ an $S$-linear map. Then there is a small nonempty directed set $I$ with diagrams of local homomorphisms $R_i	o S_i$, local transition maps $r_{ji}:R_i	o R_j$, $s_{ji}:S_i	o S_j$, and local cocone maps $R_i	o R$, $S_i	o S$, commuting with all ring squares. There are finitely presented $S_i$-modules $M_i,N_i$, maps $u_i:M_i	o N_i$ linear over $S_i$, additive transitions $m_{ji},n_{ji}$ semilinear over $s_{ji}$, and additive cocone maps $\mu_i:M_i	o M$, $
u_i:N_i	o N$ semilinear over $S_i	o S$. All transitions are identities at equal indices and respect composition; all cocones are compatible. Moreover $n_{ji}u_i=u_jm_{ji}$ and $
u_i u_i=u\mu_i$. The following hold. (1) $R_i$ and $S_i$ are Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; $R_i$ is essentially of finite type over $\mathbf Z$, and $S_i$ is essentially of finite type over $R_i$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. (2) $R=\varinjlim R_i$, $S=\varinjlim S_i$ as rings and $M=\varinjlim M_i$, $N=\varinjlim N_i$ as abelian groups [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. These are algebraic colimits: every element is represented at a stage, and two stage elements have equal images exactly when their images agree at a common later stage. (3) For $i\le j$ the canonical map $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j	o S_j$, $s\otimes r\mapsto s_{ji}(s)r$, is a localization at a multiplicative subset, and the canonical maps $M_i\otimes_{S_i}S_j	o M_j$ and $N_i\otimes_{S_i}S_j	o N_j$, $x\otimes s\mapsto s\,m_{ji}(x)$ and $y\otimes s\mapsto s\,n_{ji}(y)$, are isomorphisms. (4) For each $i$, $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R	o S$ is a localization, and $M_i\otimes_{S_i}S	o M$, $x\otimes s\mapsto s\mu_i(x)$, and $N_i\otimes_{S_i}S	o N$, $y\otimes s\mapsto s
u_i(y)$, are isomorphisms. The isomorphisms in (3) and (4) carry $u_i\otimes1$ to $u_j$ and $u$, respectively. Here a localization at $W$ means that all $w\in W$ become units, all target elements are fractions with denominators in $W$, and an element maps to zero only if some $w\in W$ kills it; tensor products are as in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. All sets and rings may be placed in one common sufficiently large universe.

proof.text: Apply the local tower theorem to R→S→S and M, with the identity as the second map. Its hypotheses follow from the given localization presentation and finite presentation of M. Write the output R_i→B_i→S_i with module models T_i. Apply the supplied-tower collapse lemma to these exact diagrams: it gives Noetherianity, essential finite type of R_i→S_i, and the canonical transition and limit localizations. The tower statement supplies finite cokernel presentations for T_i and canonical identifications T_i⊗S≅M.

proof.text: Pass from the supplied directed preorder to its antisymmetrization. Choosing representatives gives a final functor back to the preorder, so the top ring cocone remains a colimit. Use the object clause of affine module descent to model both M and N at stages, after replacing each limit module by its finite-presentation small representative. Move the two models to a common upper stage by scalar extension, which preserves finite presentation. Conjugate u by their limit identifications and use the morphism clause to descend it to a further stage c. Transport the canonical-colimit result to the supplied cocone using its unique ring isomorphism and the extension-restriction equivalence. Thus P,Q over S_c and v:P→Q have fixed identifications S⊗P≅M and S⊗Q≅N carrying 1⊗v to u.

source.place: Tag 05N7 (lemma-colimit-category-fp-modules), clauses (1),(2); Tag 00QX, tensoring the finite presentation.

proof.text: Restrict to j≥c and apply the fixed-arrow scalar-extension diagram theorem to (S_i), P,Q,v. Its specified formulas supply the module transitions, arrow squares, finite presentations, canonical transition/limit isomorphisms, and algebraic group colimits. Compose its limit cocones with the fixed identifications to M,N; these send v⊗1 to u, so they give exactly the displayed canonical maps and equations. The tail is final: an upper bound of any i and c lies in it. Final-tail colimit invariance retains both ring colimits. Their algebraic element criteria persist because any representing or equality stage can be advanced to an upper bound with c. Locality, Noetherianity and ring localization comparisons simply restrict. Thus every requested clause holds on this tail, in a common sufficiently large universe. To preserve the independent module universe, apply Mathlib Algebra.FiniteType.small to the finite type integer subalgebra of each essentially finite type stage ring. Its submonoid and their product are small; IsLocalization.mk'_surjective and small_of_surjective show that the localized stage ring is small in the requested universe. Finite stage modules are small by Module.Finite.small. Use Shrink with its transported module structure and linear equivalence, and conjugate every diagram map and comparison. Use Mathlib Types.FilteredColimit.isColimitOf with the transported representative and eventual equality criteria to construct the colimits of underlying types. A proved private lifting lemma for any filtered category upgrades a colimit of underlying types to an additive-group colimit: the universal descending function is additive because any two elements have representatives at a common stage; IsColimit.ofFaithful supplies factorization and uniqueness. The argument handles independent index and group universes and changes no statement.
